acceptance_criteria.criterion: ADR-009 is committed under docs/decisions and fully specifies byte-level encodings for every supported type, object keys, ordered collections, unordered collections, and all rejected values.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/decisions/0009-canonical-encoding.md defines the closed value domain, tags N/T/F/I/B/S/O/L/U, framing, UTF-8 encoding and ordering, collection semantics, stable rejection codes, and version policy.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: CanonicalEncoder output conforms to ADR-009 and is deterministic for repeated encoding of the same logical value.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: packages/core/src/canonical-encoder.mts implements the specified tags and framing; repeated and insertion-permuted nested-value tests passed in the 101-test automated run.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Objects or maps with identical entries but different insertion order produce identical bytes, with keys ordered by their UTF-8 byte sequences rather than locale-sensitive comparison.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Object and Map entries are sorted with compareBytes over utf8Encode(key); UTF-16/UTF-8 divergence, locale-sensitive, normalization-form, and insertion-permutation tests passed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Unordered collections with identical logical members but different insertion order produce identical bytes; ordered collections preserve order and produce different bytes when element order differs.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Set members are sorted by complete encoded bytes while arrays are emitted by index; corresponding insertion-independence and order-sensitivity tests passed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Values that are logically distinct by supported type or structure do not share an encoding in the required collision-separation test corpus, including bigint versus safe integer and ordered versus unordered collections.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Distinct tags separate scalar and structural forms. The 27-value uniqueness corpus and focused bigint/integer, scalar/list, list/set, key/value, and null/boolean/string tests passed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Encoding rejects undefined, NaN, positive and negative Infinity, negative zero, unsafe integers, unsupported runtime values, and cyclic structures with deterministic typed errors.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: CanonicalEncoderError exposes stable codes for each rejection category; automated tests passed for all required numeric cases, undefined, representative unsupported values, unsupported keys, malformed strings, and object/array cycles.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No StateHash or SaveHash implementation is introduced by this change.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The changed implementation exports only canonical encoding APIs, error definitions, value types, and an encoding-version constant; no hash implementation or hash dependency was added.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Core sources pass the repository typecheck, lint, determinism lint, and package-boundary checks.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Automated validation passed npm lint and all 101 tests; npm test runs the compile pretest and the repository boundary/config/lint suites. The implementer additionally reports successful standalone compile, lint, and boundary commands.

invariants_checked: INV-22 canonical representation and type/structure separation
INV-26 package architecture and dependency boundaries
UTF-8 byte ordering independent of locale and UTF-16 ordering
Typed deterministic rejection of prohibited values and cycles
No floating-point arithmetic or rounding behavior added
No validation weakening, skipped tests, retries, or tolerance loosening identified
No temporary or debug artifacts identified
risks: Encoding very large bigint or deeply nested inputs remains proportional to input size and nesting depth; this is inherent to the accepted unbounded value domain and is not a task regression.
payload.summary: The candidate defines ADR-009, implements the documented deterministic canonical encoding domain, provides substantive golden/order/separation/rejection coverage, introduces no hashing, and passes the relevant repository gates without unrelated scope expansion.
